info.name: Axiom v1.0.0 API
info.description:
Manual API testing/documentation collection for Axiom v1.0.0 -- a secure server-side automation/action agent for Linux servers.

This collection is a testing artifact only. It does not ship with Axiom and does not affect its runtime/API behavior.

Axiom's entire API surface is four endpoints, all covered here:
- GET  /health
- POST /v1/actions/{action}
- GET  /v1/jobs/{job_id}
- GET  /v1/jobs/{job_id}/logs

EVERY request in this collection (except /health, if your agent has security.health.allow_anonymous: true) requires mutual TLS: a client certificate signed by the CA your Axiom agent trusts. Postman cannot express a client certificate inside collection/request JSON for security reasons -- you must configure it separately in Postman's app-level Settings > Certificates (per-domain), matching {{base_url}}'s host. See docs/postman-testing.md in the repository for the full walkthrough, including this limitation.

No certificates, private keys, or credentials are included in or required by this file. No company-specific hosts, IPs, or project names are used -- every environment-specific value is a collection variable you fill in yourself.

Postman here is a manual/exploratory testing client standing in for a real caller (e.g. a Jenkins pipeline) -- it calls the exact same four endpoints documented in docs/jenkins-integration.md.

variable.description: Base URL of the Axiom agent you're testing against, including port. Replace with your own agent's address -- this placeholder resolves nowhere. The client certificate you configure in Postman's Settings > Certificates must be attached to this exact host.

Name of an action to trigger. 'backend.deploy' is a common example name from this project's docs (see configs/example.yaml) -- it must actually exist in the config.yaml of the Axiom agent you're pointing at, and your client identity must be allowlisted for it, or you'll get 404/403 respectively.

Example value for a declared 'image_tag' action parameter, matching the pattern used in this project's example config (^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,128}$). Only relevant if the action you're triggering actually declares an image_tag parameter -- Axiom rejects any parameter an action hasn't declared.
Populated automatically by the 'Trigger Action' request's test script after a successful (202) trigger. You can also set this manually to check on a job triggered elsewhere.

For the 'Unauthorized Action' negative test: a real, configured action name that your client identity's allowlist does NOT include. Adjust to match your own config.yaml's authorization.identities section.

For the 'Nonexistent Action' negative test: an action name that does not exist in the target agent's config at all. The default value is unlikely to collide with a real action name, but adjust if needed.

request.description: GET /health. Authenticated by default -- requires the same client certificate as every other endpoint unless the target agent has security.health.allow_anonymous: true in its config. Expect {"status":"ok","agent":"<agent-id>","version":"..."}.

exec: pm.test('response has expected health fields', function () {

request.description:
POST /v1/actions/{action}. Triggers a configured action and returns immediately with a job_id -- the action itself runs in the background.

IMPORTANT: '{{action}}' must already exist as a named action in the target Axiom agent's config.yaml, and your client certificate's identity must be listed under that action in authorization.identities -- Axiom does not accept arbitrary action names or commands. See docs/actions.md in the repository for the action model.

The request body's 'parameters' object may only contain parameter names the action has actually declared in its config (e.g. 'image_tag') -- an undeclared parameter, or one that fails its configured regex pattern, is rejected with 400 before the action ever runs. If the action takes no parameters, send an empty body or {}.

On success (202), the test script below saves job_id into the job_id collection variable automatically, ready for the 'Get Job Status' and 'Get Job Logs' requests.

// instead, see the Negative Tests folder for what each means -- this
// script only asserts/extracts on the success path.
pm.test('response has job_id and queued status', function () {

request.description:
GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}. Run 'Trigger Action' first (or set {{job_id}} manually) so this has a real job to look up.

Status is one of: queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled. Poll this on an interval (e.g. every 5-10s) until it reaches a terminal state (succeeded/failed/cancelled) -- see docs/jenkins-integration.md for the polling pattern a real CI caller uses.

404 means either the job_id is wrong/malformed, or the Axiom agent has restarted since the job ran -- job history is in-memory only and does not survive a restart (see docs/INSTALL.md section 11); the audit log is the durable record instead.

exec: pm.test('response has expected job fields', function () {

item.name: Negative Tests (security model)
item.description: Each request here is EXPECTED to fail with a specific status code -- that's the point. Use these to manually verify Axiom's default-deny authorization, mTLS enforcement, and parameter validation without writing any code. None of these send a dangerous or arbitrary-command payload -- Axiom has no endpoint that would accept one in the first place (see docs/security.md).

request.description: Expect 401. Postman attaches a client certificate per-domain from Settings > Certificates, not per-request -- there is no in-collection way to send 'this one request without the cert'. To actually run this test, temporarily remove/disable the client certificate for this host in Postman's settings, run this request, then re-add the certificate before continuing with the rest of the collection. See docs/postman-testing.md for the exact steps -- this is the main Postman/mTLS limitation to be aware of.

exec: pm.test('status is 401 when no client certificate is presented', function () {

request.description: Expect 403. Uses {{unauthorized_action}} -- a real, existing action name that your client certificate's identity is deliberately NOT allowlisted for in the target agent's config.yaml (authorization.identities). This demonstrates default-deny: a valid, CA-trusted certificate is not enough on its own.

exec: pm.test('status is 403 for a non-allowlisted action', function () {

request.description: Expect 404. Axiom only recognizes actions explicitly declared in the target agent's config -- there is no arbitrary-command endpoint, so an unrecognized name is simply 'not found,' never executed.

exec: pm.test('status is 404 for an action that does not exist', function () {

request.description: Expect 400. Sends an empty parameters object against an action that declares at least one required parameter (e.g. 'image_tag: required: true' in the example config) -- adjust {{action}} to point at such an action in your own config if the default doesn't declare one.

exec: pm.test('status is 400 for a missing required parameter', function () {

request.description: Expect 400. The example config's image_tag pattern is ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,128}$ -- spaces aren't allowed, so this value fails validation before the action ever runs. This is a benign example chosen only to violate the pattern; it is not an injection payload and does not need to be (Axiom never passes parameter values through a shell in the first place -- see docs/security.md).
